Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The two commands `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will only fetch sources and parse the PKGBUILD without executing build() or package() functions. The source is fetched from a legitimate GitHub URL (github.com/SagerNet/sing-box) pointing to the official upstream repository. The sha256sums, while containing a single expected checksum, will only be used for verification during build (which is blocked by --nobuild).

The PKGBUILD uses standard packaging practices: variable substitution for source URLs, proper variable declarations, and standard Go build commands. The _pkgver transformation using sed is a common pattern for handling version strings with prerelease suffixes (alpha/beta/rc) that upstream uses. These commands execute during source fetch and PKGBUILD parsing phases only, not during build/package phases where the actual binaries are created and installed.

No malicious network requests, obfuscated code, or dangerous operations are present in the top-level scope or pkgver() function. The source URL is correctly pointing to a legitimate upstream project repository.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>Legitimate upstream source fetch with standard PKGBUILD practices</summary>
</security_assessment>
